EUR-AUD:

ORFL Up & True demand

Close up on a 1-min chart for detail:

Let's look to see where price was reacting to...I will extend the black line over to the right for reference on chart below.

Here is a close up of the red FL Box where price reacted. There are three main points of interest, the engulf, RT, and new high.

Before I go any further on EA, I want to investigate an important reaction that I missed before. Here is a higher time frame chart that shows the main areas I already analyzed in previous posts. # 1 is a reached target, # 2 is a reached target, but I need to see if the TG at # 3 was reached. In order to do this I need to look at a LTF chart.

Here is the HTF view first:

Here is a close up of the area. I drew the ORFL down and the true supply zone. The neon green line shows where price bounced/reacted. The reaction broke the true supply zone but it did not break the ORFL - Down.

It looks like an engulf of true supply...

If you read this from a higher time frame perspective, it is possible that this was an engulf of TS, and price deeply RT before heading on to reach the target for longs above.

If we go off the theory that price did indeed engulf TS, then we need to analyse why price RT to the place it did before moving up to hit the target of the engulf (target for longs above). The chart below shows the areas where price retraced before moving up. Like Salivan always asks: "Where is price coming from?" Well, at Point "X" we would say price is coming from an unreached target for longs. This should keep us focused on taking long trades. We would also be anticipating tricks for IT's to load buy orders.

Next, lets look to see what the target for longs would be (look above the EG of the TS area). We know where the ultimate target ended up (thanks to the benefit of hindsight) but we should look closely to see how it moved to the target. First, I see a different target that price needed to reach first. Take a look at the chart below. a little bit above the engulf was another reaction with a true supply zone.

Here is the zone:

The TS located in the green shaded rectangle is the first target for the original upside engulf of the TS located below. We have to wait and see how price reacts to this new TS level before deciding whether the IT's intend to push price further up, or drop it back down.

Here is a LTF chart showing the detail of how I drew the zone:

And...you can see price engulfs this new TS zone...IT's intentions are higher. We expect a RT with some tricks being played. Where is price coming from? Still, it is coming from an unreached target for longs.

Continued from post above: EUR-AUD:

I am having a harder time understanding why price broke up to the level it did before dropping.... The PA is messy and I need to look further to the left to see what important areas were engulfed.

Here is a more detailed look at the entire area. All this PA is located within a HTF FL Box (this is important in terms of scale). Each engulf of an area of TS/TD gives us an indication of where price wants to travel next. Then we can look for the deepest possible area of RT before price forms some tricks and continues on to hit its target.

If you look at the red circle in the chart below, you will see where it reacts to the left. I can't seem to identify the reason why this level is important...although it does look like one of those QM MPL bounces that I don't understand...

Here is a close up of the possible QM zone... the PA is messy and hard to read here. I am guessing where the TS is located...just based on how price reacts to the level, but I can't explain why it is there...or where the ORFL is located.

And it brings me back to this question:

What if price engulfs the extreme of the ORFL located at the distal portion of the FL Box? Does that effect how we read this as a FO vs. EG?

Price has three important structures that can be engulfed or FO:

1. FL Box Itself 2. ORFL 3. True Supply/Demand & Its associated MPL

Scenario # 1: Price engulfs only True Supply:

Scenario # 2: Price engulfs both TS and ORFL

Scenario # 3: Price engulfs TS, ORFL, and the FL Box. In this scenario, price has broken in to a different zone. Is this significant? Salivan always mentions the importance of a FO to another FL... is this what he means

If this is right, and price breaking all levels creates a FO to a new FL, then is this the accurate drawing? Price FO and when price returns to the MPL of True Supply, it turns.

Going back to EUR-AUD, it does appear that price FO to a different FL...price bounces at the pink dotted line...which is in the vicinity of the QM level and MPL of TS.

(Continued from post above)

If I am right about the QM level reaction, the next question is: how do we know the spike is a FO vs. EG?

It isn't as simple as looking where the FO occurred to see if it happened in an important area for FOF. There is more to it, and I think it has everything to do with scale and targets. These QM's don't always hold... There is a reason for this.

As Salivan says: Where is price coming from?

The answer to that question will let us know if the QM will hold.

Hi Jurij -

I totally agree...I would only go long at the trap area with a tight stop. In my opinion, the risk is that price will RT back to the scale ORFL - UP. It is a QM level...I think you identified the same level in your charts too.

A disciplined trader would just wait for the deep RT & go long at the QM.

The question about whether price will RT beyond the QM level....I don't have a good answer for that, other than I don't think it will drop further than the QM level without first hitting the target for longs above.

The real issue is how to identify the edge of the "zone". IF says " If the signal is given by the market mover (an engulf into a new zone), then price is very unlikely to break the extreme of the zone it just came from

I think 'zone' is PAZ, and I think the PAZ has something to do with the FL Boxes. In this case, the QM level is formed within a 'Origin up' that was created as the result of price engulfing an ORFL (origin down). This new 'origin up' is at the edge of the zone....so price can RT to this extreme before going higher (in the direction of the engulf) There just so happens to be a really nice QM level at this extreme...perfect place to bounce price. Seeing a LTF DM form just above the QM level would be even more perfect.

All that being said, it would have been nicer if price had made a new high to break the previous high that forms the top of the blue box I drew....that hasn't happened yet. Still, Salivan says the only true engulf is an engulf of TS/TD...so technically we do have a valid HTF engulf indicating price wants higher...

If we ask "where is price coming from" we can say it is coming from a unmet target for longs...which tells us three things:

1. We need to look for buys 2. We need to expect tricks to occur when price RT 3. The RT will occur to the extreme set of orders left in the zone

If you were an IT, you would want to make the engulf of TS look like a FO so traders would be focused on shorting. You would be gradually buying in to all those shorts. They would see the engulf of TS as a FO and the FO of the QM below as an engulf...You would trick everyone to taking the wrong side, leaving yourself the only one with buys.

I like the QM level for a long... the R:R would be giant.

H, I like your answer and I think if we consider the engulf you marked (true supply eng) then the extreme zone is the QM as you pointed out. What makes it a bit confusing is the engulf on daily scale where the extreme edge of the PAZ would be that blue daily FL I think. Anyway, keeping an eye on that QM, in case we get the RT

As always nice posts and many things to think about
